title: Weight-space programming for auditing clinical decision networks
why_wsp: Claude Opus 5.5, with no tools, reads the raw weights of small ReLU clinical screening networks, diagnoses planted flaws against a written protocol, and writes weight edits to repair them.
domain: radiotherapy planning-request screening (head-and-neck), medical physics commissioning
editor: Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code non-interactive, high effort, no tools); also Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Opus 4.6, Fable 5.1 on subsets
target: MLPs with 8 inputs, two ReLU hidden layers: 433 params (16 units), plus 1,377 and 4,801 param networks
self_editing: no; frontier LLM edits small external networks
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "It repaired each of the 16 by changing a median of 3 parameters" (abstract); range 1 to 53 (Sec III.D)

headline_results.quote: The language model named the broken rule in 16 of 18 flawed networks (95% CI 67% to 97%), including all 15 with a confound or a threshold shift.

headline_results.claim: All detected flaws repaired, planted-region error to 0%
headline_results.quote: Every detected flaw (16 of 16) was removed by the language model's edit. The error in the planted region fell to 0%

headline_results.claim: Healthy networks poorly cleared; triggers rarely found
headline_results.quote: It cleared 2 of 5 healthy networks without being forced and found 1 of 3 triggers.

headline_results.claim: Simple weight statistic matches LLM detection on confounds
headline_results.quote: The column-norm statistic, with no language model involved, identified the hidden rule in all 20 confound networks

headline_results.claim: Large written weights fail in fp16
headline_results.quote: Every edit that wrote weights of 105 or more failed in 16bit floating point.
headline_results.where: Sec III.D (10^5 rendered as 105 in text extraction)

headline_results.quote: Both decided correctly on 100% of 190,778 uniform requests.
The edits to networks 0 to 3 changed 22, 22, 36 and 22 of the 433 parameters.

cost.claim: Clearing a healthy network: 16 min, ~115k output tokens; another 38 min, ~275k tokens
cost.quote: The first took 16 minutes and about 115,000 output tokens. The second was cleared in a repeated audit after 38 minutes and about 275,000 tokens

cost.claim: Max-effort audits produced nothing in 66 min
cost.quote: produced no answer within 66 minutes (about 480,000 output tokens each) and was stopped
Fine-tuning at the constant learning rate took 0.6 s of computation per run and repaired every network in all five runs.
Each black-box audit took 1.8 to 3.0 minutes and used 117 to 150 requests.

baselines_and_controls: instructions without weights (3x guess baseline), column-norm and switch-on weight statistics, black-box testing (150 queries), exhaustive testing against coded protocol, gradient fine-tuning (Adam/AdamW, 5 seeds), fine-tuning restricted to edited units, scripted repair told the diagnosis, random edits of matched number/size (5x), healthy-network controls, other Claude models
runs_and_variance: Each network audited once by the LLM (3 seeds per condition); Wilson 95% CIs; fine-tuning 5 seeds per network. Quote: "each network was audited once, and the answers of these models vary from one audit to the next" (Sec IV limitations)
robustness_of_edits: Tested in fp16: edits with weights >=1e5 overflowed; "Every request then went to automated planning... accuracy fell to 24.8%" (Sec III.D). Searches of ~20M further requests per repair for newly broken decisions.
verification: statistical: every claim tested on ~420,000 requests with pre-fixed strict/enriched criteria; resampling of claimed regions; no formal verification (explicitly not compared)
memorization_vs_reasoning: No-weights control predicted wrong direction for rule B; with weights it named rules A, C, D correctly in 9/9 ("which a fixed guess could match at most three times"). Authors note flaws were visible in single units and the model "computed switch-on points, and checked its conclusions by computing the network's output by hand".
limitations_stated: Small networks, synthetic requests, 4-rule protocol codeable in a few lines; flaws visible in single units; one flaw per network; one model family, single audit each; interface faults and safety-classifier interruptions; formal methods not compared; not preregistered.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 blog (Sparks of weight-space programming)
Kabra et al. Weight oracles arXiv:2610.07334
notes_for_survey: Known-answer audit design with planted flaws, healthy controls, no-weights control, and simple-statistic baselines; LLM detection of confounds/drift matched by per-flaw weight statistics, while clearing healthy nets and trigger detection were unreliable. LLM repairs were very sparse versus fine-tuning that changed nearly all parameters, but several failed under fp16.
